lines.text: Your agents live in a terminal on one laptop. Close the lid, and the work stops.
Agent R Q runs your agents on any machine you own. And it starts them from the browser.
Ada adds her dev box in two commands. Install the daemon, then enroll it with a one-time code.
The daemon connects, and the card turns green, with its C P U and memory.
Storefront has no agent, so its page offers one. Start it in its folder, on the dev box.
She picks Claude Code, with Opus and high effort.
The machine starts it, and its terminal opens right in the browser, live.
Seconds later, storefront turns green, ready for tasks.
A waiting task can get an agent of its own. Spin up forks the workspace, and starts a second agent there.
When an agent needs you, a toast finds you on any page. With push on, it reaches you with the tab closed.
And for work you trust, Always Allow turns one yes into a rule. Every call stays on the record.
Your machines, your agents, from any browser. Where would you run your agents? Tell us in the comments, and try it at Agent R Q dot com.
